updates.name: James H. Mather
updates.bio: Atmospheric scientist at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory who joined DOE's ARM program in 1994 as a Penn State postdoc and moved to PNNL in 2001. Directed the ARM user facility from 2007, leading a team of over 300 spread across nine DOE laboratories and other institutions; had recently retired as director per an August 2026 PNNL item.

updates.name: Carl A. Roland
updates.bio: Plant ecologist with the National Park Service at Denali National Park and Preserve since 2000, and principal investigator for the Central Alaska Network's vegetation monitoring and plant inventory, which also covers Wrangell-St. Elias and Yukon-Charley Rivers. Listed papers address boreal and treeline vegetation change, plant and lichen diversity, wildfire and spruce. Holds an M.Sc. in botany from UAF.
updates.research_interests: boreal forest and treeline vegetation change; plant and lichen diversity and floristics; wildfire effects on boreal vegetation; spruce growth and climate sensitivity; long-term vegetation monitoring in interior Alaska parks
updates.current_title: Plant Ecologist, Denali National Park and Preserve
updates.evidence: Denali plant ecologist and principal investigator for Central Alaska Network vegetation monitoring program

updates.name: Wayne R. Munns
updates.bio: Scientist with the U.S. EPA for nearly 30 years, including more than 12 years as director of the Narragansett, Rhode Island laboratory now named the Atlantic Coastal Environmental Sciences Division, and later senior science advisor at EPA's Center for Environmental Measurement and Modeling. Published widely on population-level ecological risk assessment and on bringing ecosystem services into decisions. Died June 2026.
updates.research_interests: population-level ecological risk assessment; ecosystem services in environmental decision-making

updates.name: Christopher J. Korleski
updates.bio: Per a 2022 conference biography, head of the EPA's Great Lakes National Program Office since August 2011, apart from 2016-2018 leading EPA Region 5's Water Division. Earlier he directed the Ohio EPA (2007-2011), was in-house environmental counsel for Honda of America and worked on environmental enforcement for the Ohio Attorney General. Trained in soil science and law.
updates.evidence: Chris Korleski became director of U.S. EPA’s Great Lakes National Program Office (GLNPO) in August 2011.

Nebraska 1984, law degree Ohio State 1987. updates.name: Philip R. Kaufmann
updates.bio: Holds a courtesy appointment in Oregon State University's Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Sciences. Works on stream channel form and hydraulics, sediment transport and its effects on biota, natural and human influences on aquatic habitat, field methods for measuring biota and habitat, and physical habitat structure in streams, rivers and lakes. PhD in forest hydrology, Oregon State University, 1987.
updates.research_interests: stream channel form and hydraulics; quantitative field methods for aquatic biota and habitat; natural and human controls on aquatic habitat and biota; stream sediment transport and its biological effects; physical habitat complexity in streams, rivers and lakes
updates.current_title: Courtesy appointment, Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Sciences
